Test-optional since 2013; choose on the Common App whether scores are considered; self-reported scores accepted, official only if enrolling

Yes, meets 100% of calculated need (packages can include loans and work). Brandeis Commitment for domestic students: full tuition covered at family income up to $75,000, half tuition $75,001-$200,000 (typical assets), from fall 2025 entrants

Domestic applicants: FAFSA plus Faye (Brandeis's own aid tool). CSS Profile (code 3092) for international, undocumented/DACA and noncustodial-waiver cases. Aid forms due Nov 2 (ED I/EA) or Jan 15 (ED II/RD); must indicate aid intent on the application

Yes; named merit scholarships (Presidential, Trustee, Justice Brandeis, Dean's, MLK, Bernstein and others), renewable for 8 semesters with no GPA requirement. ED applicants eligible too. No separate merit application found
About $97,758 for 2026-27 on campus plus travel (tuition $73,080, activity fee $598, avg housing $13,180, food $8,700, books $1,000, personal $1,200); one-time new student fee $450 domestic
ED I Nov 2 (decision Dec 15), non-restrictive EA Nov 2 (Feb 1), ED II Jan 15 (Feb 15), RD Jan 15 (Apr 1). ED I and ED II are binding and need the ED Agreement; aid offer is the same as RD

Admissions interviews only for international students, by invitation; internationals encouraged to use InitialView or Vericant (ED I by Nov 15, ED II/RD by Jan 15). collegedata.fyi's copy of CDS 2025-26 lists interview as 'considered'
Admission is to the university, not a major; students declare by the end of sophomore year. Independent interdisciplinary major and dual BA/MA options

No Brandeis writing questions on a standard domestic first-year Common App for 2026-27; extra prompts only for international applicants and Myra Kraft Achievers program applicants. Brandeis does not publish them on its own site

Gap: third-party sources disagree on the 2026-27 international-applicant prompt ('What excites you the most about being an international student at Brandeis University?' vs a new 'learning beyond the classroom' prompt), so it is left out. Also: two recommendations required (counselor and core-subject teacher); $80 fee
